title.zh: 轴对称磁通导出极向场

summary: Recover radial and axial poloidal magnetic-field components and their magnitude from axisymmetric flux on a rectilinear cylindrical R-Z grid.

identity.relation: axisymmetric flux psi = R A_phi to poloidal magnetic field
identity.direction: R-Z grid and psi -> B_R, B_Z and B
identity.definition: Recover BR=-dZ(psi)/R and BZ=dR(psi)/R using nonuniform quadratic stencils written as local value differences. A constant flux gauge differentiates exactly to zero. At a regular axis use BR=0 and BZ=2*(psi(R1)-psi(0))/R1².
identity.model: axisymmetric cylindrical poloidal-field relation with discrete grid derivatives
identity.geometry: rectilinear R-Z mesh, optionally including the cylindrical axis
identity.boundary: At an included R=0 column, use the stated axis rule; at other grid edges, use one-sided second-order derivatives.
assumptions: psi denotes R A_phi in Wb/rad, with R and Z in metres. The maintained circular-filament and current-Green vacuum-field contracts use the same normalization; full linked flux is 2*pi*psi.
The sampled flux is sufficiently resolved for the finite-difference derivative to represent the intended field.
Adding an extremely large gauge can destroy the represented flux variation before this function is called; the derivative cannot recover lost input bits.

inputs.name: r_grid
inputs.description: Cylindrical radius at each grid point.
inputs.constraints: Finite rectilinear grid with nonnegative, strictly increasing R axis and N_R >= 3; same shape as z_grid and psi.

inputs.name: z_grid
inputs.description: Axial coordinate at each grid point.
inputs.constraints: Finite rectilinear grid with strictly increasing Z axis and N_Z >= 3; same shape as r_grid and psi.

inputs.name: psi
inputs.description: Axisymmetric poloidal flux function R A_phi sampled on the R-Z grid, not full linked flux.
inputs.constraints: Finite values and exactly the same two-dimensional shape as the coordinate grids.

outputs.name: B_R
outputs.constraints: Zero at an included cylindrical-axis column.

outputs.name: B_Z
outputs.constraints: Uses the discrete axis rule if R=0 is included.

outputs.name: B
outputs.constraints: No fixed lower floor is applied.

preconditions: Axisymmetric psi, R and Z share the declared SI units and [Z,R] indexing.
The grid has at least three strictly ordered points along each coordinate axis.
supported: Discrete reconstruction of an axisymmetric poloidal field on a finite rectilinear R-Z grid, including the maintained R=0 rule.
excluded: Automatic conversion of full linked flux into psi=R A_phi; callers must divide full linked flux by 2*pi before using this operator.
A general proof of axis regularity or derivative convergence for arbitrary flux data.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for wrong rank or shape, nonfinite coordinates or psi, nonrectilinear or insufficient grids, decreasing/repeated axes, or negative starting radius.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Unexpected NumPy arithmetic errors propagate. Finite accepted inputs are not guaranteed to yield finite derivatives when floating-point range is exceeded; no output-finiteness gate is applied.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iteration is performed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No dictionary is returned if validation fails or execution raises.

example.description: Recover a uniform axial field from a quadratic flux profile including R=0.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import poloidal_field_from_flux
r_grid, z_grid = np.meshgrid([0.0, 0.2, 0.4], [-0.5, 0.0, 0.5])
result = poloidal_field_from_flux(r_grid, z_grid, r_grid**2)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['B_R'], 0.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['B_Z'], 2.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['B'], 2.0)
example.expected: B_R is zero and B_Z = B = 2 T at every point, including the cylindrical axis.

scope: Quadratic-flux uniform-field and axis-rule regression on uniform and selected nonuniform grids.
A 2*pi rescaling of the psi input rescales the recovered axial field in a controlled quadratic example; full linked flux must be divided by 2*pi to recover psi=R A_phi.
Finite subnormal and large-magnitude hypot helper regression.
Constant psi=3.7 produces exactly zero field for three distinct grids.
A representable strong constant gauge on a manufactured even flux leaves BR/BZ invariant, including the axis.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Manufactured and analytic discrete checks establish only the stated poloidal model and declared integration geometry. Arbitrary Green matrices, pressure closures, experimental plasma applicability and public release are not established by these tests.
known_limitations: Caller-supplied physical closures and Green responses require their own evidence and coherent psi=R A_phi (Wb/rad) normalization.
Floating-point rounding envelopes do not bound discretization error or experimental uncertainty.
No expert scientific endorsement or public release follows from this numerical successor.
